question: Which products had the most customers in Q1 2026?
sql_query:
WITH scoped AS (
      SELECT oi.id AS item_id, oi.order_id, oi.user_id, oi.product_id,
             oi.sale_price, oi.created_at AS purchased_at,
             p.brand, p.category, p.name AS product_name 
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi
      JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders` o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND o.user_id = oi.user_id
      JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` p ON p.id = oi.product_id
      
      WHERE (@all_brands OR p.brand IN UNNEST(@allowed_brands)) AND oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') AND o.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
    ) SELECT product_id, product_name, ROUND(SUM(sale_price), 2) AS revenue,
           COUNT(*) AS units, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS customers,
           COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders, CAST(MAX(purchased_at) AS STRING) AS latest_purchase
        FROM scoped WHERE DATE(purchased_at) >= @start AND DATE(purchased_at) < @end
        GROUP BY product_id, product_name ORDER BY customers DESC, product_id, product_name LIMIT 10
analyst_report: Illustrative method: rank distinct customers separately from revenue; break ties by product ID. On the synthetic test fixture, product 3 has four customers versus product 1 with one. These are not live company figures.
definitions: v1: revenue=sum(item sale_price); units=item rows; customers=distinct user_id; orders=distinct order_id. Both order and item status exclude Cancelled/Returned. Dates use order_items.created_at, UTC [start,end). Current status, not historical snapshots.

question: Did inactivity increase between May and June 2026?
sql_query:
WITH scoped AS (
      SELECT oi.id AS item_id, oi.order_id, oi.user_id, oi.product_id,
             oi.sale_price, oi.created_at AS purchased_at,
             p.brand, p.category, p.name AS product_name 
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi
      JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders` o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND o.user_id = oi.user_id
      JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` p ON p.id = oi.product_id
      
      WHERE (@all_brands OR p.brand IN UNNEST(@allowed_brands)) AND oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') AND o.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
    ), boundaries AS (
          SELECT @start AS as_of UNION ALL SELECT @end AS as_of
        ), histories AS (
          SELECT as_of, 'all' AS cohort, user_id,
                 MIN(DATE(purchased_at)) AS first_purchase,
                 MAX(DATE(purchased_at)) AS last_purchase
          FROM scoped CROSS JOIN boundaries
          WHERE DATE(purchased_at) < as_of
          GROUP BY as_of, cohort, user_id
        ), summary AS (
        SELECT CAST(as_of AS STRING) AS period, cohort,
          COUNT(*) AS eligible_customers,
          COUNTIF(last_purchase < DATE_SUB(as_of, INTERVAL @inactivity_days DAY)) AS inactive_customers,
          SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(last_purchase < DATE_SUB(as_of, INTERVAL @inactivity_days DAY)),
                      COUNT(*)) AS inactivity_share
        FROM histories
        WHERE first_purchase < DATE_SUB(as_of, INTERVAL @inactivity_days DAY)
        GROUP BY period, cohort
        ), selected AS (
          SELECT cohort FROM summary GROUP BY cohort
          ORDER BY MAX(eligible_customers) DESC, cohort LIMIT 50
        )
        SELECT summary.* FROM summary JOIN selected USING (cohort)
        ORDER BY cohort, period LIMIT 100
analyst_report: Illustrative method: compare eligible/inactive counts at two as-of boundaries before explaining a spike. In the synthetic fixture, the share increases from 0/1 to 5/5. Examine denominator maturation, label causal explanations as hypotheses, and do not count other-brand purchases.
definitions: v1: revenue=sum(item sale_price); units=item rows; customers=distinct user_id; orders=distinct order_id. Both order and item status exclude Cancelled/Returned. Dates use order_items.created_at, UTC [start,end). Current status, not historical snapshots. Churn proxy: 90-day inactivity share at start/end (exclusive as-of). Eligible = first authorized purchase before as-of minus N days; inactive = last purchase before that cutoff. Empty denominator is undefined. Not newly churned customers in a month. Brand breakdown capped at 50 largest eligible cohorts, preserving both snapshots.

question: Create Q1 insights and Q2 actions.
sql_query:
WITH scoped AS (
      SELECT oi.id AS item_id, oi.order_id, oi.user_id, oi.product_id,
             oi.sale_price, oi.created_at AS purchased_at,
             p.brand, p.category, p.name AS product_name 
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi
      JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders` o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id AND o.user_id = oi.user_id
      JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` p ON p.id = oi.product_id
      
      WHERE (@all_brands OR p.brand IN UNNEST(@allowed_brands)) AND oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') AND o.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
    ) SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE(purchased_at)) AS month, ROUND(SUM(sale_price), 2) AS revenue,
           COUNT(*) AS units, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS customers,
           COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders, CAST(MAX(purchased_at) AS STRING) AS latest_purchase
        FROM scoped WHERE DATE(purchased_at) >= @start AND DATE(purchased_at) < @end
        GROUP BY month ORDER BY month LIMIT 10
analyst_report: Illustrative method: clarify year, compare total and monthly revenue, then product/customer concentration. Pair each action with evidence, a proposed owner and a proposed success measure. Additional fresh queries are needed; this single query is one step, not a complete report.
